question: What cervical measurement tells us that the second stage of labor has officially started?
explanation: The second stage begins when the cervix is fully open at ten centimeters. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h1)

question: What main activity sets the second stage of labor apart from the first stage?

options.B: Initial engagement of the fetal head
options.C: Active pushing and delivery of the baby
options.D: Separation and delivery of the placenta

explanation: The first stage focuses on opening the cervix, while the second stage centers on pushing the baby down and out. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for causing strong uterine contractions in the second stage?
explanation: Oxytocin stimulates the muscle of the uterus to trigger and maintain powerful contractions. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does Ferguson's reflex help a mother during the second stage of labor?

options.A: It numbs the area to decrease labor pain
options.B: It relaxes the abdominal muscles to reduce tiredness
options.C: It causes an involuntary urge to push when the baby presses low
options.D: It prevents heavy bleeding by contracting blood vessels

explanation: Pressure from the baby's head on the pelvic floor sends signals that release oxytocin and create a natural urge to bear down. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h2)

question: What does a bulging perineum during the second stage of labor tell us?

options.A: The placenta is starting to separate
options.B: The amniotic membranes have ruptured early
options.C: Extra fluid has gathered in the lower uterus
options.D: The cervix is fully open and the baby is moving down

explanation: As the baby's head moves deep into the pelvis, it presses directly against the perineum, causing it to bulge outward. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following physical changes is NOT typically seen as the baby moves down onto the pelvic floor?

options.B: The cervix goes back down to two centimeters

explanation: By the time these signs happen, the cervix is already fully open at ten centimeters and has pulled back completely over the baby's head. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h3)

question: What happens during the movement called flexion as the baby travels through the pelvis?

options.A: The baby's chin tucks tightly against its chest
options.B: The baby's head turns sideways to face the hip
options.C: The baby straightens its legs to add pushing force
options.D: The shoulders turn to fit the pelvic outlet

explanation: Flexion helps the smallest part of the baby's head lead the way through the birth canal. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why must internal rotation happen during normal labor?

options.A: To let the placenta detach safely from the uterine wall
options.B: To help the baby line up with the widest part of the lower pelvis
options.C: To keep the umbilical cord away from the neck
options.D: To trigger the mother's body to release oxytocin

explanation: Internal rotation turns the baby's head so it can navigate the curves of the lower pelvis. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h4)

question: When is the best time to check the baby's heartbeat during the second stage of labor?

options.A: Only at the very beginning of pushing
options.B: Every ten minutes regardless of contractions
options.D: While the mother is actively pushing

explanation: Checking the heartbeat right after a contraction helps catch any drops in oxygen caused by labor stress. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h5)

question: A midwife sees thick green meconium in the amniotic fluid as the baby's head crowns. What is the most important first step?

options.A: Give oral oxytocin to speed up the birth
options.B: Ask the mother to stop pushing and rest for two hours
options.C: Get equipment and team ready for possible newborn resuscitation
options.D: Do an immediate instrumental delivery before checking vitals

explanation: Thick meconium can mean the baby experienced stress and might breathe in fluid, so being ready to care for the newborn right away is essential. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h5)
